title: The 1/3–2/3 conjecture
formal: Does every finite partially ordered set that is not a total order have incomparable elements x and y such that between one third and two thirds of its linear extensions place x before y?
context:
The probability is with respect to the uniform distribution on linear extensions.

This question was found through Wikipedia and compared individually with the existing candidate and archived records. The linked literature provides definitions and background; this import is not a completed research-card review.
why: Would provide a universally informative comparison for sorting with partial-order information; retained as a computationally motivated combinatorial exception.
